name: Sea Pavilion — surface and detail kit
prompt:
Create ONE clean detailed GAME ASSET REFERENCE SHEET, NOT Blender or a3Dmodel. Plain light ivory studio background, soft even light, full uncropped separate objects, readable thickness, precise non-melting forms. FULL IDs and names outside silhouettes, dimensions marked PROPOSED. Each cell independent illustration scale. No environment scenery, humans, extra unlabeled objects, watermark or whole-palace redesign. Use ONLY the single supplied source image for visible style/material/form authority; infer missing backs and assembly interfaces conservatively. Source illustration motifs are inspiration, not recovered measured geometry. Visible source facts: Very open seaside pavilion under a turquoise glass/shell canopy with multiple pointed petal lobes, gold ribs, nacre columns/screens and central shell basin. It is not the same circular glass dome as B20. Hidden layout inference: A short shore/dock approach reaches a compact shell courtyard, visitors pass around the basin to a sea-facing balcony and return around the open edge. Keep slender bays and water view unobstructed; a few marine planters soften the landing without filling the hall. Preserve this local design. Exactly12 isolated main components in a clean4-column grid. No missing/empty slots or repeated subjects counted twice. One clear front/three-quarter view with useful small rear/top/contact inset per cell. Truly flat backs for appliques, square join ends for repeat mouldings. Screens have repeated coherent holes, no tangled tendrils. Windows separate glass from surrounds, cornices/parapets and posts separate where named. Do not include large room/scenery fragments attached to a tiny detail. Title "B23-DETAIL-001 — Sea Pavilion — surface and detail kit". Footer "Proposed construction / source-compatible references / mesh joins and views unverified".

Purpose/gap: Need petal-roof/rib springing modules, nacre column/corner seats, shell-screen end joints and shore-platform threshold. Existing shell basin and jali motifs are source vocabulary; use shared water/dock/rocks. Coastal vines/planters/seaweed and reef fish/shorebirds proposed. Missing detached construction pieces and local interior-facing patterns.
